paragraphs.source_en: They found Sax and Frank bunched before one screen, Yeli and Ann and Simon before another. A UNOMA satellite was tracking Phobos with a telescope, and Sax was measuring the moon's speed of passage across the martian landscape to get a fix on its velocity. In the image on the screen Stickney's dome shone like a Faberge egg, but the eye was drawn away from that to the moon's leading edge, which was blurry and streaked with white flashes of ejecta and gases. "Look how well balanced the thrust is," Sax said to no one in particular. "Too sudden a thrust and the whole thing would have shattered. And an unbalanced thrust would have set it spinning, and then the thrust would have pushed it all over the place."
